title: Provisioning Sentry: Prefetch Region Selection and GPU-class Budget Guardrails
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Customers occasionally experience sudden cost spikes or elevated latency when we route inference requests into regions or accelerator classes that become expensive due to spot churn or SKU pricing changes. Current routing policies favor lowest-cost end-to-end but lack a fast preflight step to identify transient capacity risks and enforce per-tenant spend caps. Goal: Implement a lightweight 'Provisioning Sentry' layer that prefetches capacity and price signals for candidate regions/GPU classes, scores them with tenant-specific budgets and performance SLOs, and applies soft+hard budget caps with graceful model-variant degradation when necessary. The feature should be policy-driven, observable, and reversible at runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Provisioning Sentry returns a scored shortlist of candidate (region, gpu_family) pairs within 50ms for 95% of calls
Per-tenant spend guards enforced: soft_limit triggers best-effort mode, hard_limit rejects or routes to fallback with clear error code
Fallback chain executes without increasing 95th-percentile latency above baseline by more than 20%
Feature toggle and canary rollout available in console with traffic split and dry-run mode
Automated tests cover scoring logic, budgeting paths, and model-variant fallback execution
design_notes: Prefetch model: maintain a short-lived snapshot (<=10s TTL) of region and instance-class capacity estimates and spot-price deltas from cloud telemetry
Scoring factors: estimated token-throughput, median latency from last-minute telemetry, spot-eviction-risk heuristic, unit-price, and tenant budget headroom weighted by policy

Budget semantics: tokenized budget accounting (tokens * cost-per-token) with a two-tier cap: soft_limit (probabilistic throttling / degrade to cheaper model variant) and hard_limit (rejects or routes to paid-on-demand pool)
GPU-class selection: classify into families (A: high-memory low-cost, B: high-FP throughput expensive). Use GPU affinity overrides for customers with explicit hardware requirements
Fallback model variants: pre-registered chain in order [full-precision -> quantized-8 -> quantized-4 -> small-variant], preserve semantic constraints via eval thresholds
Policy configuration: per-tenant YAML/JSON policy with fields: preferred_regions, region_tier_weights, soft_budget_pct, hard_budget_pct, gpu_family_whitelist, fallback_chain
Failure modes: stale prefetch data results in suboptimal route; mitigate via short TTL and secondary metric (recent latency) fallback
tradeoffs: Prefetch adds extra RTT if executed synchronously; mitigate by integrating into routing decision path with cached snapshots and background refresh
Conservative scoring may reduce peak cost savings but improves stability; will default to conservative until telemetry validates
Adding budget logic increases route rejection risk; use soft-degrades and clear UX messaging before hard blocks
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Data collectors - extend telemetry pipeline to export per-region capacity estimate and spot-price deltas (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Scoring service - implement Provisioning Sentry microservice with in-memory TTL cache and scoring algorithm (3 weeks)
Phase 3: Router integration - wire scoring results into runtime router with policy evaluation and fallback execution paths (2 weeks)
Phase 4: Console/Policy UI - expose per-tenant budget caps and dry-run controls in Redwood Console (1 week)
Phase 5: Canary rollout - dry-run at 1% traffic, then ramp to 20% with simulator-backed validation, then GA (2 weeks)
Phase 6: Post-launch tuning - adjust weighting, eviction heuristics, and add more telemetry signals (ongoing)
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring weights and budget accounting logic
Integration tests: inject synthetic spot-price spikes and verify routing decisions and fallback chain
Load tests: validate 95th-percentile decision latency under 5000 qps routing load
Chaos test: simulate regional evaporation (zero capacity) and confirm graceful degradation
Canary simulation: run historical traffic through dry-run mode compare cost and latency to baseline
monitoring_and_alerting: Metrics: sentry_decision_latency_ms, sentry_cache_hit_rate, per_tenant_soft_budget_trigger_rate, per_tenant_hard_budget_rejects, fallback_usage_rate
Dashboards: per-region cost delta, GPU-family selection distribution, 95p latency impact when fallback applied
Alerts: >=5% of requests hitting hard_limit in 15m for a tenant -> page on-call SRE; sentry decision latency >200ms sustained -> page
rollout_steps: Create feature flag and default to off for all tenants
Enable dry-run for internal tenant and run 100% traffic through sentry without affecting routing
Open canary for select low-risk tenants with configurable soft/hard caps
Monitor metrics and perform two-way comparisons on cost and latency
Gradually enable for broader tenants with opt-out and additional logging for first 72h
config_examples:
policy: {
  preferred_regions: ["us-west1", "us-central1"],
  region_tier_weights: {"us-west1": 1.0, "us-central1": 0.8},
  soft_budget_pct: 65,
  hard_budget_pct: 95,
  gpu_family_whitelist: ["A100", "T4"],
  fallback_chain: ["fp32-full", "q8", "q4", "small"]
}
example runtime decision log: PREFETCH_OK region=us-west1 gpu=A100 score=0.82 soft_hit=false hard_hit=false selected=true
risks: Over-eager routing to on-demand hurts cost targets
Inaccurate capacity estimates leading to routing thrash
Complex policy surface may confuse customers; need sensible defaults
mitigations: Conservative defaults: prefer stability over raw cost savings for first month
Short TTL and circuit-breaker for prefetched data, fall back to latency-only routing when stale
Provide pre-built policy templates in Console and clear documentation for admins
